questions.question: We’ve been reading through the book of Exodus, a word which means what?
questions.answer: Exit.

questions.question: Why would they want to exit Egypt?
questions.answer: They were slaves.

questions.question: What was it?
questions.answer: To lead God’s people out of Egypt.

questions.question: But when Moses told Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, to let God’s people go, what did the stubborn king say?
questions.answer: I don’t know the Lord, so no!

source.filename: OT 30 Lesson (The Tenth Plague and Passover)(1).odt

questions.question: But even after suffering all these dreadful wonders, what did Pharaoh say?
questions.answer: No.

source.filename: OT 30 Lesson (The Tenth Plague and Passover)(1).odt

questions.question: What did Moses say would happen?
questions.answer: The firstborn son in every Egyptian home would die.

source.filename: OT 30 Lesson (The Tenth Plague and Passover)(1).odt

questions.question: Why?
questions.answer: Parents crying after losing a child.

source.filename: OT 30 Lesson (The Tenth Plague and Passover)(1).odt

questions.question: But what about God’s people, the Israelites? What did Moses say would happen?
questions.answer: They wouldn’t be harmed; not even a dog would bark at them.

questions.question: What things did God tell them to eat?
questions.answer: Roasted lamb, bitter plants, bread without yeast.

source.filename: OT 30 Lesson (The Tenth Plague and Passover)(1).odt

questions.question: What were they to do as they ate?
questions.answer: Tuck their coat into their belt, wear sandals, hold their walking stick, and eat quickly.

source.filename: OT 30 Lesson (The Tenth Plague and Passover)(1).odt

questions.question: If he saw blood on the edges of a house’s door, what did God promise to do?
questions.answer: Pass over that house, not strike down the firstborn.

source.filename: OT 30 Lesson (The Tenth Plague and Passover)(1).odt

questions.question: What does the Bible say?
questions.answer: There was loud crying because someone had died in every house.

questions.question: Why?
questions.answer: Because he saw the blood of the lamb on the door.

questions.answer: His son had died.

questions.question: But after the death of his firstborn son, what did Pharaoh say to Moses?
questions.answer: Go! Take everything and leave.

questions.question: Why would the Egyptians want the Israelites to leave?
questions.answer: So the plagues would stop.

source.filename: OT 30 Lesson (The Tenth Plague and Passover)(1).odt

questions.answer: Gold, silver, and clothing.

questions.question: What happened to the Egyptian houses during the tenth plague?
questions.answer: The firstborn son died.

questions.question: And the lamb? What did that remind them of?
questions.answer: The blood of the lamb on the door.

source.filename: OT 30 Lesson (The Tenth Plague and Passover)(1).odt

questions.question: What did the Israelites need to be saved from?
questions.answer: Slavery in Egypt.

source.filename: OT 30 Lesson (The Tenth Plague and Passover)(1).odt

questions.question: How many of us have done it?
questions.answer: Everyone, including you and me.

source.filename: OT 30 Lesson (The Tenth Plague and Passover)(1).odt

questions.question: What punishment do we earn because of our sin?
questions.answer: Death.

source.filename: OT 30 Lesson (The Tenth Plague and Passover)(1).odt

questions.question: How were the Israelite sons saved from the destroying angel?
questions.answer: By the blood of the lamb on their doorframes.

questions.question: What did God want the Israelites to remember?
questions.answer: How God rescued them from being slaves in Egypt with mighty power.

questions.question: What did God do to save us?
questions.answer: Sent Jesus to die for our sins and rise from the dead.

questions.answer: The Passover.

questions.answer: That’s how God told the people to eat the Passover.

questions.question: Why?
questions.answer: Because after 430 years in Egypt, including many years as slaves, God’s chosen people were on their way to freedom!

The Egyptians gave the departing Israelites gold, silver, and clothing.
The Israelites left Egypt so quickly that they could not finish preparing bread.
